interest: From routine approvals to refusing a Japanese ship at Davao, 1940–41.
overview: This file consists of six consecutive sheets (Sheets 16 through 21) of the Department of State's docket control 'List of Papers' for decimal file 894.3311B, indexing official correspondence and inter-departmental clearances between January 1940 and June 1941 concerning proposed visits of Japanese naval, transport, and merchant marine training vessels to ports in the Philippine Islands (primarily Manila and Davao) and Honolulu, Hawaii. The indexed records encompass diplomatic notes from the Japanese Embassy, communications from the War, Navy, and Interior Departments, and telegrams from the U.S. High Commissioner to the Philippine Islands, Francis B. Sayre. While requests in 1940 for vessels including the oiler Shiriya, transport Hayatomo, fleet oiler Iro, and training cruisers Katori and Kashima to replenish provisions and land unarmed crews were systematically approved and extended usual courtesies, the file documents a notable policy shift in May and June 1941, when the State and Navy Departments coordinated to reject a proposed visit of the training vessel Lac Maru to Davao as 'inconvenient at the present time.'
